# CHRONIC BACTERIAL PROSTATITIS

Chronic bacterial prostatitis usually presents as recurrent urinary tract infections with the same bacterial etiology. Pain, tenderness, and fever may accompany intermittent episodes of cystitis, but men are usually asymptomatic between episodes and the prostate examination may be normal. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) often relieve pain. If the diagnosis is uncertain or if the patient's symptoms do not respond to therapy, consult urology. The presence of hematuria may be a sign of carcinoma, especially in older men, and a urology consult should be requested.

A urine culture should be performed in all patients to guide antimicrobial therapy. [Chronic prostate pain syndrome](chron-pros-pelvic-pain-syn) should be considered in patients who have symptoms of prostatitis but have negative urine cultures. Chronic prostate pain syndrome is discussed elsewhere:
Chronic prostate pain syndrome

## Duration

4 weeks minimum and up to 6 weeks of treatment is required. Durations longer than 6 weeks may be needed in treatment of resistant organisms. Treatment with trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole requires a treatment duration of 1 to 3 months.

Therapy:
## Inpatient

Preferred:
Levofloxacin 750 mg PO q24h ($) [R,DI] for 4 weeks
< OR >
Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h ($) [R,DI] for 4 weeks

Alternative:
Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h ($) [R,DI] for 4 weeks

## Outpatient

Preferred:
Levofloxacin 750 mg PO q24h ($) [R,DI] for 4 weeks
Non-VA order for above

Alternative:
Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h ($) [R,DI] for 4 weeks
